items.title: 52240_Frank _Machito_ Grillo oral history interview
items.q: It wasn't yet the late Kennedy and Martin Luther King, there was nothing.

ctx.x: Roseland is still the finest ballroom in the whole world, so they was considered what Machito could be a good thing all year because we are going to enrich our clientele with all the type of people. So when we started at Palladium, naturally, the people that was there they don't know us because that was a ballroom dances; so really I was disgusted because I was success(ful) practically in every part that we appear and you get used to see a lot of people when you work, so that we were kind of, you know, gee. I…

said the guy: yes, yes, certainly, and then I didn't think twice to what I am going to say, I was younger, and I said: Are you prejudiced? He said: "No, Machito, how could I be prejudiced when your band is all black people and Spanish people. How could I be prejudiced? If I was prejudiced, you won't be here". I say: Okay, I had an idea, why we don't change the policy of mixing up. It wasn't yet the late Kennedy and Martin Luther King, there was nothing.
Yeah, there was no integration yet.
